WHERE A TECH IS RESEARCHED, AND WHERE IT IS SHOWN, ARE TWO DIFFERENT PLACES.
The owner's ruling: 'upgrades are action tiles on buildings, tech tree on mini
map is only a visual guide letting you know what buildings hold what upgrades.'
So `researched_at` is the button's home and the tech-tree page is a reference
with nothing to press -- which is what TechTreePanel has said about itself since
it was written.
AN EFFECT KEY IS `stat.scope`, and every one of the seven stats below names a
lookup the sim ALREADY makes per use. That is the whole rule and it is what
keeps a tech from needing retroactive surgery on units that already exist:
attack_damage.melee    flat, added to a unit's attack_damage (CombatSystem)
attack_damage.pierce   flat, same, for units whose attack_type is pierce
armor_melee.all        flat, subtracted from an incoming melee blow
armor_pierce.all       flat, same, for pierce
attack_range.pierce    flat tiles, widening a ranged unit's reach
gather_rate.<kind>     PERCENT, on the rate per 100 ticks (GatherSystem)
carry_cap.all          flat, on how much a worker can hold
ability_amount.<heal|damage>  flat, on what an ability heals or hits for
FOUR STATS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT and each is absent for its own reason, which
is worth reading before adding a tech that wants one:
unit_hp, building_hp, speed -- all copied onto the entity at spawn, so a tech
would either miss everything already built or need a pass that rewrites live
entities and decides what happens to their current hp.
los -- since 12.1f the CLIENT computes its own fog from `vision_range`, so a
sight tech has to reach two implementations that must never disagree.
build_rate -- BuildSystem.BUILD_RATE is 1 progress per builder per tick, and a
percentage has nothing to round to below +100%: 1 * 125 / 100 is 1. A build
tech wants that counter running at a finer granularity first, which changes
what `build_time_ticks` means in every building in buildings.json.
COMBAT TECHS SKIP WORKERS, resolved in TechMods rather than declared here. A
villager's attack_type is melee, so an unscoped +4 would take her from 3 damage
to 7 and make twenty villagers an army. AoE does not arm the peasants either.
THE MILL LADDER AND THE FIELD LADDER BOTH APPLY. `buildings.json` gives a field
gather_yield_per_age 25/28/32, which PLAN.md has described since it was written
as 'standing in for a mill tech until 9.3 lands'. It is not replaced: the age
ladder is the base and horse collar multiplies it, exactly as it multiplies
hand-gathered food. Both go through GatherSystem.harvest_rate, which is the one
place either number is read.
NUMBERS ARE AoE II's SHAPE, NOT ITS ARITHMETIC. Three tiers of +1/+1/+2 on the
attack lines and 15-20% on the gather lines are starting values, tuned by
playtest like every other number in this directory.
ICONS: there are none, deliberately. The owner asked for 'blank action tiles
with only labels filled' and the art is queued as asset_request.md [P8]. An
action with no icon and no payload draws its label, which for a tech is the
only thing that would identify it anyway.
